report.summary: Analyzed chunk 2 of 3 of mint.py, covering _show, _read_worktree, _resolve_sha, _short_hash, MUST_INCLUDE_CAP, _diff_magnitude, _diffed_symbols, _in_scope_modules, and _mint_from_diffs (partial). Checked docstring and comment claims against code.
risks: _resolve_sha | medium | Returns None on empty output from _git, but _git can also return None; _resolve_sha calls .strip() on None, causing AttributeError. | Check if _git returns None and handle before .strip().
todos: Verify _resolve_sha handles None from _git before calling .strip()

handoff.purpose: Implement helpers for diffing symbols and the core _mint_from_diffs function that builds a quarantined task from file diffs.

symbols.name: _show
symbols.note: Runs git show to get blob contents at a ref.

symbols.name: _resolve_sha
symbols.note: Resolves a git ref to a SHA via rev-parse.

symbols.name: _short_hash
symbols.note: Computes a 12-char hex digest from parts.

symbols.name: MUST_INCLUDE_CAP
symbols.note: Maximum number of labels in must_include (25).

symbols.name: _diff_magnitude
symbols.note: Counts +/- lines in a unified diff between before and after source blocks.

symbols.name: _diffed_symbols
symbols.note: Returns dict mapping symbol name to diff magnitude for symbols whose extracted source differs.

symbols.name: _in_scope_modules
symbols.note: Returns frozenset of in-scope modules from cached index.

symbols.name: _mint_from_diffs
symbols.note: Builds a quarantined task from file diffs, scoped and cross-file-labeled.

claims.text: Blob contents of ``rel`` at ``ref``, or ``None`` if it didn't exist there (distinct from an empty-but-present file, which is a real "").
claims.why: The implementation calls _git and returns its result; this chunk does not contain _git, so whether it returns None on non-existence cannot be verified.

claims.text: Current on-disk contents of ``rel``, or ``None`` if it's gone (deleted by the edit being minted).
claims.why: Code returns read_text result, catches OSError and returns None.

claims.text: Deterministic size proxy for one symbol, used only to rank which labels survive ``MUST_INCLUDE_CAP`` -- NOT a precision diff.
claims.why: Function computes a count of +/- lines in a unified diff with n=0, which is deterministic and coarse.

claims.text: A pure add or remove counts its whole body; an in-place edit counts only the lines that moved.
claims.why: The unified diff with n=0 will show all +/- lines for added/removed files; for edits, only changed lines appear. The count sums all +/- lines.

claims.text: Matched by NAME against a (name -> sorted source list) map rather than a single name->source dict, so duplicate names (same-named methods on sibling classes, nested closures) don't silently clobber each other and under-report a real change.
claims.why: Code builds before_map and after_map where each name maps to a list of sources (via setdefault), then sorts and compares lists.

claims.text: A file with no language spec (unsupported extension) contributes nothing -- there is no unit-level ground truth to diff, only whole-file text, and this module deliberately doesn't fall back to that (a whole-file "changed" label would be far too coarse to be an honest must_include).
claims.why: Function returns {} if spec_for(rel) is None.

claims.text: The magnitude is only ever used for cap-ranking in ``_mint_from_diffs``; it plays no part in WHETHER a symbol counts as changed (that's the ``!=`` comparison below).
claims.why: Changed dict is built only when before_srcs != after_srcs; magnitude is computed only for changed symbols.

claims.text: The scope membership test -- ``rel in modules`` -- exactly as slice.py uses it for its own neighborhood expansion (slice.py, ``rel not in modules`` around line 225).
claims.why: This chunk does not contain slice.py; cannot verify the claim about slice.py usage.

claims.text: Degrades to an empty scope (so callers mint nothing rather than crash) on ANY indexing failure -- minting must never raise on a caller looping over commits, same contract as ``_git``.
claims.why: Function catches Exception and returns frozenset() on any failure.

claims.text: ``files`` keys not present in ``in_scope`` are excluded from BOTH target and label consideration entirely -- they never reach ``_diffed_symbols`` at all, so an out-of-scope file that would raise/misbehave under unit-level parsing (a minified bundle, say) can never even get that far.
claims.why: Code builds skipped list and then scoped dict by filtering files not in in_scope; only scoped files are passed to _diffed_symbols.

claims.text: ``diagnostics["skipped_out_of_scope"]`` is always present (sorted, maybe empty).
claims.why: Line 89: diagnostics = {"skipped_out_of_scope": skipped} with skipped sorted.

claims.text: ``diagnostics["reason"]`` is present only when ``task`` is ``None``.
claims.why: In the chunk, reason is set in all paths that return None (lines 101-104, 117-122, 134-136, 156-162). No path that returns a task sets reason.

claims.text: The task's ``target`` (the anchor the slicer will be pointed at) is, among in-scope files that have at least one diffed symbol, the one that still EXISTS after the edit with the most diffed symbols, ties broken by path for determinism -- a deleted file cannot be a slice target.
claims.why: The code selects anchor from existing (non-deleted) files when possible; only when all files are deleted does it fall back to per_file. The docstring's claim about 'still EXISTS' is mostly upheld.

claims.text: A single changed symbol in the anchor earns symbol-level precision (``target::symbol``); more than one keeps the target file-level.
claims.why: This chunk does not contain the part of _mint_from_diffs that constructs the task dict with target string; the code stops before that.

claims.text: ``must_include`` is every diffed symbol in every OTHER in-scope touched file (never the anchor's own), capped at ``MUST_INCLUDE_CAP`` keeping the largest-magnitude symbols (``must_include_dropped`` records how many were cut, so a capped task never silently reads as full coverage).
claims.why: Code builds cross_file_sizes from per_file items excluding anchor. Then ranks and caps at MUST_INCLUDE_CAP, computes dropped count. The chunk does not show must_include_dropped being recorded in diagnostics, but the cap and drop computation is present.

claims.text: If _is_linked_worktree(repo_root) is true, minting is refused with a specific reason.
claims.why: Lines 95-105: if _is_linked_worktree(repo_root): sets reason and returns None, diagnostics.

claims.text: FLOOR-TRIPPING LABEL SOURCE EXCLUSION -- a floor-tripping file can't be pointed at (semantic_slice's FOCUS GATE fails it closed).
claims.why: Code computes floor_tripped list and excludes those files from anchor_pool. If anchor_pool is empty, returns None with reason.

claims.text: The same file is withheld as a NEIGHBOUR in every lane too, so its symbols can never be recalled.
claims.why: In the cross-file loop, lines 140-144: if rel in floor_tripped: labels_filtered_secret_floor.update(sizes); continue – symbols from floor-tripped files are excluded from cross_file_sizes.

claims.text: JUNK / CROSS-LANGUAGE / SECRET-FLOOR filtering happens per (file, name) occurrence, BEFORE the max-magnitude merge -- a name filtered out of one file's occurrence can still be kept from another (matching-family, non-junk, non-floor-tripping) file's occurrence.
claims.why: The loop iterates over each (rel, sizes) and for each name checks junk, cross-language, floor-tripped before merging into cross_file_sizes via max. So filtering is per occurrence.

claims.text: If not cross_file_sizes, label hygiene filtered every cross-file candidate; minting returns None with diagnostics.
claims.why: Lines 156-162: if not cross_file_sizes: sets diagnostics with filtered lists and reason, returns None, diagnostics.

observations.what: _resolve_sha calls .strip() on the return value of _git, but _git could return None, causing AttributeError.
In _mint_from_diffs, when existing is empty, anchor_pool falls back to per_file which may include deleted files, contradicting the docstring's claim that a deleted file cannot be a slice target.

The floor_tripped check uses scoped[rel][1] or '' for deleted files; if a file is deleted, after_text is None, so '' is used. This may cause secret_floor_rule to incorrectly trip on a deleted file that would not have tripped if its content were present.
